profile.summary: Swiss family-controlled group that leads both biologic drugs and in-vitro diagnostics, built around full ownership of Genentech (2009) and majority control of Japan's Chugai (2002). Since 2000 it has shed flavours (Givaudan), vitamins (to DSM) and consumer health (to Bayer) to focus on prescription medicines and diagnostics, and keeps adding platforms such as Foundation Medicine, Flatiron, Spark and obesity assets.

events.description: Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche founds the company in Basel to make branded, industrially produced medicines.
Chugai Shinyaku, founded in Tokyo in 1925 by Juzo Ueno, takes the name Chugai Pharmaceutical.
Robert Swanson and Herbert Boyer found Genentech, the first recombinant-DNA biotech company.
Genentech sells Corning a 6.5% stake and the two create industrial-enzyme joint venture Genencor.
Roche buys about 60% of Genentech, gaining control while leaving it publicly listed and independently run.
Roche acquires worldwide rights to the polymerase chain reaction, a cornerstone of its molecular diagnostics business.
Roche buys Palo Alto drugmaker Syntex, which becomes Roche Bioscience.
Roche Biomedical Laboratories, its US clinical lab chain, is sold to National Health Laboratories.
Purchase of Corange, parent of Boehringer Mannheim, creates Roche Diagnostics as a global diagnostics leader.
Orthopaedics unit DePuy, owned through Boehringer Mannheim/Corange, is sold to J&J.
Roche spins off its fragrances and flavours division, owned since 1963, as Swiss-listed Givaudan.
Nippon Roche merges into Chugai, giving Roche a 50.1% stake in a still-listed, autonomously run Japanese drugmaker.
Before the Roche alliance takes effect, Chugai spins off its wholly owned US diagnostics unit Gen-Probe.
Roche Venture Fund is set up; it is now a CHF 750M evergreen fund backing pharma, diagnostics and digital-health startups.
Roche completes the sale of its vitamins and fine chemicals business, with about CHF 3.4B in sales, to DSM.
Roche Consumer Health (non-prescription drugs) is sold to Bayer for about CHF 3.6B, closing at year-end.
Genentech's first major takeover, an all-cash buyout of Xolair co-developer Tanox.
Roche buys tissue-diagnostics leader Ventana, founding its pathology and companion-diagnostics franchise.
Roche buys the Genentech shares it did not already own, making it a wholly owned subsidiary.
Acquisition of InterMune brings Esbriet for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
Genentech buys Seragon's oral SERD breast-cancer programs, plus up to $1B in contingent payments.
Roche takes a 56.3% majority stake in genomic-profiling company Foundation Medicine via tender offer and new shares.
Purchase of precision-oncology biotech Ignyta, owner of ROS1/NTRK inhibitor entrectinib (Rozlytrek).
Roche buys oncology real-world-data company Flatiron Health, a former Roche Venture Fund holding.
Roche acquires the remaining 42.5% of Foundation Medicine, taking full ownership.
Foundation Medicine is founded in Cambridge, Massachusetts, building on Broad Institute cancer-genomics work.
Spark is founded to commercialize gene therapies developed at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia; Luxturna follows in 2017.
After a long FTC review, Roche closes its cash takeover of gene-therapy pioneer Spark.
Roche adds GenMark's multiplex syndromic molecular testing for infectious diseases.
Roche buys Roivant/Pfizer-owned Telavant and US/Japan rights to TL1A antibody for inflammatory bowel disease.
Purchase of Carmot gives Roche incretin-based obesity and diabetes candidates.
Genentech's Vacaville, California biologics plant is sold to contract manufacturer Lonza.
Roche agrees to buy allogeneic CAR-T developer Poseida, a long-standing partner.
Roche closes its purchase of 89bio and MASH drug pegozafermin: $14.50 per share plus up to $6 CVR.
Agreement to buy AI digital-pathology firm PathAI ($750M upfront plus $300M milestones); expected to close in H2 2026.
